title: Deep Neural Networks for Securing IoT Enabled Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
authors: Tejasvi Alladi, Ayush Agrawal, Bhavya Gera, Vinay Chamola, Biplab Sikdar, Mohsen Guizani
dataset: VeReMi Extension (19 attack / fault types + normal)
attacks: all 19 types (1-9 faults, 10-19 attacks) merged into one anomaly class; includes 16 GridSybil, 17 DataReplaySybil, 18 DoSRandomSybil, 19 DoSDisruptiveSybil
unit: sequence of 20 consecutive messages of one sender (as received by RSUs)
features: position x, y and speed x, y in (20 x 4); model reconstructs position (20 x 2)
model: CNN-LSTM (1-D conv, 20 filters + 4-layer LSTM, 256 units) vs stacked 4-layer LSTM, reconstruction
learning_setting: one-class (normal-only training), called unsupervised by the authors
training_data_assumption: benign only: 85% of the normal sequences, selected with the dataset's ground-truth labels; no contamination
anomaly_score: MAE between input and reconstructed sequence
threshold_selection: ON TEST DATA WITH LABELS: Algorithm 1 sweeps thresholds over the test sequences and their labels and keeps the one with maximum accuracy (sharp peak of the accuracy-vs-threshold curve); no validation set
split_protocol: 85% of normal for training; test = remaining normal + all anomaly sequences in the original class ratios; vehicle-level separation not stated
metrics_result: CNN-LSTM accuracy 0.980 (anomaly precision 0.996 / recall 0.956 / F1 0.976); stacked LSTM accuracy 0.954. Per-type recall, CNN-LSTM / LSTM: type 2 constant offset 0.892 / 0.011, type 9 eventual stop 0.519 / 0.055, type 12 delayed messages 0.636 / 0.625, type 13 DoS 0.887 / 0.753; types 16-19 (Sybil) 0.998 / 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0 (CNN-LSTM) and 0.984 / 0.989 / 1.0 / 0.997 (LSTM)
sybil_evaluated: yes: GridSybil, DataReplaySybil, DoSRandomSybil, DoSDisruptiveSybil recall 0.98-1.0
limitation_gap: threshold tuned on the labelled test set (optimistic); no AUROC; no length / message-rate control, so Sybil recall near 1.0 is not separated from shortcuts; split by vehicle not stated; weak types are reported (2, 9, 12)
relevance_why: same dataset and same four Sybil attacks with a benign-only reconstruction model; reports near-perfect DataReplay / DoS recall, the opposite of our finding, under a test-tuned threshold
verified_via: Crossref API (DOI metadata) + full text PDF (author copy, ece.nus.edu.sg) read in this session

title: PAMPOS: Causal Transformer-based Trajectory Prediction for Attack-Agnostic Misbehavior Detection in V2X Networks
authors: Konstantinos Kalogiannis, Ahmed Mohamed Hussain, Panos Papadimitratos
area: V2X misbehaviour detection, benign-only prediction-based anomaly detection
dataset: VeReMi++ / VeReMi Extension, 38 scenarios (19 attacks x afternoon / morning rush)
attacks: A1-A19 incl. A16 GridSybil, A17 DataReplaySybil, A18 DoSRandomSybil, A19 DoSDisruptiveSybil
unit: sliding window of 10 consecutive messages (stride 1) predicts step 11; sequences split at gaps > 2 s, minimum 15 messages; decision per sender
features: 8 relative kinematic features: sender-claimed minus ego (receiver) position, speed, acceleration, heading (x, y each)
model: causal transformer decoder, next-step prediction
training_data_assumption: benign only: ~13M windows from 2,735 benign senders across all 38 scenarios; benign senders identified through the dataset's ground truth (not discussed)
anomaly_score: per window: mean of the top-3 of 8 per-feature absolute prediction errors, each normalised by the benign MAE of that feature; sender score = mean over its windows
threshold_selection: fixed percentile of the benign validation sender scores (98th, tau = 4.43, 2% FPR; 411 validation senders); the cross-scenario section instead reports the 96th percentile chosen for 'optimal F1' (inconsistent)
split_protocol: by sender identity 70 / 15 / 15 train / val / test; cross-scenario afternoon <-> morning
metrics_result: AUC up to 0.98, F1 up to 0.95 for most attacks; per-attack F1: A16 0.94, A17 0.95, A18 0.95, A19 0.95; weak: A2 constant position offset F1 0.19 (recall 0.11), A9 eventual stop 0.73, A13 DoS 0.75; cross-scenario mean AUC 0.95, mean F1 0.86-0.87 (A2 0.14)
sybil_evaluated: yes: all four Sybil types, F1 0.94-0.95
limitation_gap: no head-to-head baseline (states the setups of DeepADV, SVMDformer, Campos et al. are incompatible); sequences need >= 15 messages, which removes the 1-3-message pseudonym tracks that dominate DataReplay / DoS Sybil data; sender-level decision uses the true sender; per-attack AUC not tabulated
relevance_why: closest current work: benign-only, VeReMi Extension, all four Sybil attacks, split by sender, threshold from benign validation; reports failures on A2 / A9 / A13
verified_via: arXiv abstract page + arXiv HTML full text fetched in this session

title: VehiGAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Adversarially Robust V2X Misbehavior Detection Systems
authors: Md Hasan Shahriar, Mohammad Raashid Ansari, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Cong Chen, Jonathan Petit, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou
venue: IEEE ICDCS 2024 (extended version: ACM Transactions on Cyber-Physical Systems 9(3), 2025, doi 10.1145/3745787, adds Md Shahedul Haque)
area: V2X misbehaviour detection, GAN / AE / classical one-class comparison
dataset: VASP (Veins / OMNeT++ / SUMO, Boston network): 1,018,098 benign BSMs from 475 vehicles + attack runs with 25% malicious vehicles, 2,641,309 BSMs, 35 of 68 attacks used
attacks: 35 position / speed / acceleration / heading / yaw-rate falsifications (random, offset, constant, high, low, combined); no Sybil attacks
unit: 2-D snapshot of the 10 most recent BSMs of one vehicle x 12 features (10 Hz BSMs)
features: physics-guided: delta x, delta y, vx, vy, delta vx, delta vy, ax, ay, delta heading x / y, yaw rate x / y
model: ensemble of WGAN discriminators (60 trained, top-m shortlisted, k averaged); baselines: CNN autoencoder on raw features (BaseAE) and on physics features (VehiAE), PCA, KNN, GMM
learning_setting: one-class (benign-only training) with attack-labelled validation for model selection

threshold_selection: p-th percentile (99 to 99.99) of the benign training scores; but the WGANs to ensemble are chosen by average AUROC on a validation set that contains benign and attack traces (defender assumed to hold representative attacks)
